cc.name: Rome
cc.attr: Streets, parks, rail, Tevere and Aniene: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), Geofabrik extract Dec 2023. Coast: OSM via @geo-maps. Outer rivers and roads: Natural Earth.
cc.baseOn: Base map: OpenStreetMap streets, parks and water for all of Rome inside and around the GRA, out to Ostia, Fiumicino and Maccarese (extract of Dec 2023).
cc.extrasNote: Off the planned walks: add them with Custom, or go on their own.
cc.helpNote: Base map: OpenStreetMap streets, parks and water across the whole city and the coast (Dec 2023 data). The church hunt is the heart of this map: Routes › Curated › Church hunt has five days (modern, through the ages, south-west, south-east, north). Most Catholic churches close about 12:00–16:00; San Gaspare, the Jubilee Church and Hua Yi Si stay open at midday. Pins come from Google Places where possible; a pin with a dashed ring is approximate (the place is nearby, not exactly there).

sights.name: Santa Maria Antiqua
sights.blurb: A 6th-century church inside an imperial building at the foot of the Palatine, its walls layered with paintings from four centuries.
sights.when: Forum ticket with the SUPER/Full Experience add-on; booking required; 9:30–18:00. Closed on free first Sundays.
sights.q: Santa Maria Antiqua, Foro Romano

sights.name: San Nicola in Carcere
sights.blurb: A medieval church built straight into three Republican temples; underneath, you walk the alleys between their podiums.
sights.when: Daily except Wednesday 10:00–17:00 (checked May 2026); the underground costs about €3.
sights.q: Basilica di San Nicola in Carcere, Roma

sights.name: San Clemente
sights.blurb: The textbook stack: a 12th-century church on a 4th-century church on a Roman house with a temple of Mithras.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 9:00–12:30 and 14:00–18:00, Sun 12:00–18:00 (Google, 2026); underground about €10 online, €12 at the desk, timed entry.
sights.q: Basilica di San Clemente, Roma

sights.name: Santo Stefano Rotondo
sights.blurb: Rome's oldest round church, 5th century, its walls lined with 34 lettered scenes of martyrs being tortured.
sights.when: Closed Monday; roughly 10:00–13:00 and afternoons (sources disagree: 15:30–18:30 or 14:30–17:30).
sights.q: Basilica di Santo Stefano Rotondo, Roma

sights.name: Case Romane del Celio
sights.blurb: Under the church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo: Roman apartments with a painted Christian shrine on a stair landing.
sights.when: Daily 10:00–16:00 (Google, 2026); ticket with audio guide. Entrance on the Clivo di Scauro.
sights.q: Case Romane del Celio, Clivo di Scauro

sights.name: Catacombs of Saints Marcellinus and Peter + Mausoleum of Helena
sights.blurb: A little-visited catacomb with restored frescoes, joined to the mausoleum of Constantine's mother.
sights.when: Catacomb by booking only (santimarcellinoepietro@gmail.com, +39 339 6528887); closed Thursday and 1–15 Aug, 1–15 Sep; mausoleum alone €3, joint ticket €8–10.
sights.q: Mausoleo di Sant'Elena, Via Casilina 641

sights.name: San Bartolomeo all'Isola
sights.blurb: On the Tiber island, where the healing temple of Asclepius stood: a well-head over the sacred spring and a French cannonball in the wall.
sights.when: Church hours (unchecked).
sights.q: Basilica di San Bartolomeo all'Isola, Roma

sights.name: Santa Passera
sights.blurb: A three-storey stack by the Tiber: medieval church on early-medieval crypt on a Roman tomb. There is no saint called Passera.
sights.when: Sunday Mass 10:30 (not July–September); the lower levels only on guided visits (next announced 28 Nov 2026).
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Passera, Vicolo di Santa Passera

sights.name: Santa Maria in Aracoeli: the drilled column
sights.blurb: Up 124 steps on the Capitol: a hall of reused Roman columns, one of them bored through. Was it a sundial? Probably not.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria in Aracoeli

sights.name: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
sights.blurb: Borromini's university church: a star-shaped plan and a lantern that twists into a corkscrew. Reopened October 2026.
sights.when: Mon–Fri 9:30–13:30, free (reopened 27 Oct 2026, run by Touring Club volunteers). The courtyard can be seen whenever the gate is open.
sights.q: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza, Corso del Rinascimento 40

sights.name: Sant'Ignazio di Loyola
sights.blurb: The Jesuits ran out of money for a dome, so Andrea Pozzo painted one, flat, on canvas. Stand on the floor disc and it appears.
sights.when: Daily, from 9:00 (Google, 2026); a mirror on a trolley helps you study the ceiling; queues at peak times.
sights.q: Chiesa di Sant'Ignazio di Loyola, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria dell'Orazione e Morte
sights.blurb: The church of the brotherhood that buried Rome's unclaimed dead; below, a crypt of bones with skulls labelled by date and cause of death.
sights.when: Open only by appointment through the Associazione Amici del Tevere (Turismo Roma, 2026); a restoration was under way. The façade is always there.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Maria dell'Orazione e Morte, Via Giulia 262

sights.name: Santo Spirito in Sassia
sights.blurb: Europe's oldest hospital complex: a 120 m frescoed ward, a church, a medical museum and the stone baby hatch on the street.
sights.when: The complex is by booking only (corsiesistine@aslroma1.it); the outside and the baby hatch any time. The medical museum next door keeps its own hours.
sights.q: Complesso Monumentale Santo Spirito in Sassia, Borgo Santo Spirito

sights.name: Santi Cosma e Damiano
sights.blurb: A Roman library hall turned into a church in 527, with one of the oldest apse mosaics in Rome and a window into a round temple.
sights.q: Basilica Santi Cosma e Damiano, Via dei Fori Imperiali

sights.name: San Crisogono (lower church)
sights.blurb: Under a busy tram stop in Trastevere, a whole 4th-century basilica, entered from the sacristy.
sights.when: About €3; roughly 7–11:30 and 16–19 (sources conflict); restoration was still under way in March 2026.
sights.q: Basilica di San Crisogono, Trastevere

sights.name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere (excavations)
sights.blurb: Under the church, Roman houses with round basins, plus Maderno's statue of the martyr with the cut in her neck.
sights.when: Daily 10:00–12:30 and 16:30–18:30 (Google, 2026); excavations about €2.50; not during Mass.
sights.q: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere

sights.name: Carcer Tullianum (Mamertine Prison)
sights.blurb: The state prison of ancient Rome, under a 1597 church: a hole in the floor led to the death cell.
sights.when: Daily 8:30–17:00 (Google, 2026); about €10 with a tablet guide. Very small; six people at a time in the lowest cell.
sights.q: Carcere Mamertino, Clivo Argentario 1

sights.name: Catacombs of Domitilla
sights.blurb: About 17 km of galleries on four levels, entered through a 4th-century basilica half sunk into the ground.
sights.when: Daily except Tuesday 9:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 (Google, 2026); guided only.
sights.q: Catacombe di Domitilla, Via delle Sette Chiese 282

sights.name: San Sebastiano and the Memoria Apostolorum
sights.blurb: Under the basilica on the Appian Way, a 3rd-century hall where pilgrims scratched prayers to Peter and Paul on the walls.
sights.when: Church daily 8:30–18:00; catacomb on its own guided tours (check days).
sights.q: Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura, Via Appia Antica 136

sights.name: Santa Costanza
sights.blurb: The round mausoleum of Constantine's daughter, with 4th-century mosaics of grape harvests still in the vault.
sights.when: Daily 9:00–18:00 (Google, 2026); free; bring coins for the lights.
sights.q: Mausoleo di Santa Costanza, Via Nomentana 349

sights.name: Santi Quattro Coronati
sights.blurb: A fortified monastery on the Celio, built to protect popes; inside, a 1246 chapel painted with the story of Constantine.
sights.when: Church daily from 6:30, closed midday; cloister mornings; the San Silvestro chapel by asking at the nuns' wheel.
sights.q: Basilica Santi Quattro Coronati, Roma

sights.name: Santa Prassede
sights.blurb: A 9th-century church hiding the San Zeno chapel, lined with gold mosaic and including a portrait of the pope's living mother.
sights.when: Church hours (unchecked); coin-operated lights.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Prassede, Roma

sights.name: San Bernardo alle Terme
sights.blurb: A round church made in 1598 out of a corner tower of the Baths of Diocletian, under a coffered dome like a small Pantheon.
sights.when: Mornings and late afternoons (Google, 2026), closed midday.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Bernardo alle Terme

sights.name: Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio a Trevi
sights.blurb: Facing the Trevi Fountain, the parish church of the papal palace, where the hearts and organs of 22 popes are kept.
sights.q: Chiesa Santi Vincenzo e Anastasio a Trevi

sights.name: Capuchin Crypt
sights.blurb: Six chapels decorated with the bones of about 3,700 friars; the famous one, for comparison with Via Giulia.
sights.when: Daily 9:30–12:30 and 14:30–17:30 (Google, 2026); about €10 with audio guide; cover shoulders and knees.
sights.q: Museo e Cripta dei Cappuccini, Via Vittorio Veneto 27

sights.name: Tempietto di Bramante
sights.blurb: A small round temple in a cloister, built where Peter was said to be crucified; the model for St Peter's dome.
sights.when: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 (Google, 2026); free; entrance through the Spanish Academy.
sights.q: Tempietto del Bramante, San Pietro in Montorio

sights.name: St Paul's Within the Walls
sights.blurb: The first non-Catholic church inside the walls after 1870, with Burne-Jones mosaics that give the saints the faces of Lincoln and Garibaldi.
sights.when: Mon–Fri 10:00–15:00, Sunday services (Google, 2026).
sights.q: St Paul's Within the Walls, Via Nazionale 16a

sights.name: San Gioacchino in Prati
sights.blurb: An 1890s church with an aluminium dome pierced by crystal stars, built in the years of the Eiffel Tower.
sights.when: 6:30–12:30 and 16:30–19:30 (Google, 2026). Occasional guided visits to the dome terrace (tripplus.it).
sights.q: Chiesa di San Gioacchino in Prati, Via Pompeo Magno 25

sights.name: Tempio Valdese, Piazza Cavour
sights.blurb: Rome's first church on a reinforced-concrete frame (1911–14), built by Protestants in a style meant to say "church, but not Catholic".
sights.when: Inside Tuesday 17:00–19:00 and Saturday 11:00–13:00 (Google, 2026), or ask at the office Wed–Fri 10:00–12:00 (06 3204868); concerts. The exterior any time.
sights.q: Tempio Valdese di Piazza Cavour

sights.name: Great Synagogue (Tempio Maggiore)
sights.blurb: The 1904 synagogue built where the ghetto walls stood, with the only square dome in Rome, clad in aluminium.
sights.when: Through the Jewish Museum, guided, with a security check: Sun–Thu 10:00–16:00, Fri 9:00–13:00 (Google; winter hours shorter). Closed Saturday and Jewish holidays.
sights.q: Great Synagogue of Rome, Lungotevere de' Cenci

sights.name: Sacro Cuore Immacolato di Maria, Piazza Euclide
sights.blurb: Brasini meant this church to carry a 100 m dome visible across Rome. Only the drum was built; a model of the dream stands inside.
sights.q: Basilica del Sacro Cuore Immacolato di Maria, Piazza Euclide

sights.name: Sacro Cuore di Cristo Re
sights.blurb: Piacentini's brick church of 1920–34, facing the RAI headquarters: a church halfway between tradition and the modern.
sights.q: Basilica del Sacro Cuore di Cristo Re, Viale Mazzini 32

sights.name: Santi Pietro e Paolo, EUR
sights.blurb: The domed travertine church that closes the axis of EUR, the Fascist world's-fair city.
sights.q: Basilica Santi Pietro e Paolo, EUR

sights.name: Santa Rita in Campitelli (Sala Santa Rita)
sights.blurb: A Baroque church that was taken apart and rebuilt 300 m away in 1928, when the Capitol was "cleared"; now an exhibition hall.
sights.when: Only during exhibitions, Tue–Sat 17:00–19:00.
sights.q: Sala Santa Rita, Via Montanara

sights.name: Santi Sette Fondatori
sights.blurb: A round postwar church on Piazza Salerno, white marble below and a lighter drum above.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa dei Santi Sette Fondatori, Piazza Salerno

sights.name: Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino
sights.blurb: A Fascist-era crypt of 1941 for the dead of the Roman Republic and Italian unification, under a gold mosaic vault.
sights.when: Thursday 9:30–13:30 only (from 23 Sep 2026); closes in bad weather.
sights.q: Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino, Via Garibaldi 29

sights.name: Santa Maria della Visitazione
sights.blurb: Busiri Vici's raw-concrete church in Casal Bruciato: diagonal piers and wall-beams like the ribs of a ship. The most purely brutalist church in Rome.
sights.when: Winter 7:30–12:00 and 16:30–19:00; June–August 17:00–19:00 only (Turismo Roma).
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Visitazione, Via dei Crispolti 142

sights.name: San Vincenzo Pallotti
sights.blurb: A centrally planned church of 1989–93 under a concrete hyperbolic-paraboloid vault, 900 m from the Visitazione.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Vincenzo Pallotti, Via Matteo Tondi 80

sights.name: Nostra Signora de La Salette
sights.blurb: A 1960s church on a lobed oval plan under a tent roof of fair-faced concrete that breaks the light into cones.
sights.q: Chiesa Nostra Signora de La Salette, Piazza Madonna della Salette 1

sights.name: Gesù Divin Lavoratore
sights.blurb: Fagnoni's oval church of 1955–60 for "Jesus the Worker": a stone drum on concrete piers, entered through its bell tower.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Gesù Divino Lavoratore, Via Oderisi da Gubbio 16

sights.name: San Gaspare del Bufalo
sights.blurb: One of Pier Luigi Nervi's last works: a square church entered at a corner, under a copper pyramid of prefabricated beams.
sights.when: Open 7:30–21:00 daily (Google, 2026), so a good midday stop. Metro A Arco di Travertino.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Gaspare del Bufalo, Via Borgo Velino 1

sights.name: San Giuseppe Cafasso
sights.blurb: A 1966–70 church by Paniconi and Pediconi under a massive roof that seems to float on four piers.
sights.when: Closed Monday; mostly afternoons 16:30–19:00, plus some mornings (Google, 2026).
sights.q: Chiesa di San Giuseppe Cafasso, Via Camillo Manfroni 2

sights.name: Santa Maria Madre del Redentore, Tor Bella Monaca
sights.blurb: A triangular concrete tent by Spadolini with a roof engineered by Morandi, and no cross on top: two pinnacles cut the sunlight into one.
sights.when: Parish hours; Metro C Torre Angela, then walk or bus.
sights.q: Chiesa Santa Maria Madre del Redentore, Viale Duilio Cambellotti 18

sights.name: Great Mosque of Rome
sights.blurb: Portoghesi's mosque of 1984–95, where the prayer hall is a forest of three-stemmed columns branching like palm trees.
sights.when: Visits Wednesday and Saturday mornings from 9:00 (end time 11:30 or 12:30, sources differ); not during Ramadan or holidays. Shoes off, women cover their heads, modest dress. Roma–Viterbo train to the Campi Sportivi stop.
sights.q: Grande Moschea di Roma, Viale della Moschea 85

sights.name: Dio Padre Misericordioso (Jubilee Church)
sights.blurb: Richard Meier's three white concrete sails, up to 26 m high, set among the blocks of Tor Tre Teste for the Jubilee of 2000.
sights.when: 7:30–19:00 daily (Google, 2026), so a good midday stop; no visits during Mass; free. Metro C Torre Maura, then bus 556.
sights.q: Chiesa Dio Padre Misericordioso, Largo Terzo Millennio 8

sights.name: Santo Volto di Gesù
sights.blurb: A 2003–06 church by Piero Sartogo and Nathalie Grenon, filled with contemporary art, directly across the road from medieval Santa Passera.
sights.q: Chiesa Parrocchiale del Santo Volto di Gesù, Via della Magliana 162

sights.name: San Pio da Pietrelcina, Malafede
sights.blurb: Three tilted parabolic arches of steel that touch the ground only at their ends, roofed with shards of aquamarine tile.
sights.when: 7:00–21:00 (Google, 2026). Far south-west, near the Roma–Lido line; a car or taxi helps.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Pio da Pietrelcina, Via Paolo Stoppa 12

sights.name: Hua Yi Si Buddhist temple
sights.blurb: A Chinese Buddhist temple with pagoda roofs, hidden behind warehouse walls in an industrial zone: said to be the largest in Europe.
sights.when: Daily 10:30–15:00 (Google, 2026), a good midday stop. Shoes off, quiet; men to the right, women to the left during practice.
sights.q: Centro Buddhista Hua Yi Si, Via dell'Omo 142

sights.name: Sacro Cuore di Gesù Agonizzante, Vitinia
sights.blurb: Ildo Avetta's 1955 church in a village-suburb on the Ostia railway, called one of the best Roman churches of its period.
sights.when: 7:30–19:30 (Google, 2026). Roma–Lido train to Vitinia.
sights.q: Sacro Cuore di Gesù agonizzante a Vitinia

sights.name: San Frumenzio
sights.blurb: A 1981–85 church on an elliptical plan under a tent roof with glazed gaps; it keeps the fibreglass models of Nervi's Way of the Cross.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Frumenzio ai Prati Fiscali, Via Cavriglia 8

sights.name: Santa Maria della Presentazione
sights.blurb: A concrete cylinder entered below street level, with a cross of two blades hanging like a stalactite from the dome.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Presentazione, Via di Torrevecchia 1104

sights.name: San Carlo Borromeo, Fonte Laurentina
sights.blurb: Monestiroli's tuff-clad box of 2008–10, where the tower over the altar is both bell tower and skylight.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa San Carlo Borromeo, Via Edoardo Amaldi 215

sights.name: Santa Caterina Martire (Russian Orthodox)
sights.blurb: Gold onion domes in the Russian embassy's park, looking across at St Peter's: the first purpose-built Russian Orthodox church in Rome.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Caterina Martire, Via del Lago Terrione 77

sights.name: Latter-day Saints Temple, Settebagni
sights.blurb: A North American-style temple of 2019 with two spires on a 6-hectare estate; the visitor centre is laid out like a Roman forum.
sights.when: Grounds and visitor centre Tue–Sat (Google, 2026); free. Non-members cannot enter the temple itself.
sights.q: Rome Italy Temple, Via di Settebagni 376

sights.name: San Valentino al Villaggio Olimpico
sights.blurb: A 1980s church of stacked cubes in the 1960 Olympic Village, a short walk from Nervi's viaduct.
sights.q: Chiesa di San Valentino, Viale XVII Olimpiade

sights.name: Sant'Ugo
sights.blurb: A 1989–91 parish church in Val Melaina that Italian Wikipedia counts among Rome's brutalist churches.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Sant'Ugo, Viale Lina Cavalieri 3

sights.name: Santissimo Nome di Maria in Via Latina
sights.blurb: A reinforced-concrete parish church near the Caffarella, listed among Rome's brutalist churches.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Santissimo Nome di Maria in Via Latina, Via Centuripe 16

sights.name: SS. Corpo e Sangue di Cristo
sights.blurb: Aldo Aloysi and Ernesto Vichi's 1989–91 church of exposed concrete in the Prenestino.
sights.when: Parish hours.
sights.q: Chiesa Santissimo Corpo e Sangue di Cristo, Via Narni 19

sights.name: Sacro Cuore del Suffragio and the Purgatory museum
sights.blurb: A neo-Gothic "little Milan Cathedral" by the Tiber, with one glass case of scorch marks said to be left by souls in Purgatory.
sights.when: Free; roughly 7:30–11:00 and 16:30–19:30 (sources conflict).
sights.q: Museo delle Anime del Purgatorio, Lungotevere Prati 12

sights.name: Corviale ("Il Serpentone")
sights.blurb: A single concrete housing block a kilometre long on the edge of the countryside: Rome's answer to the Falowiec.
sights.when: A lived-in building; outside and the public spaces freely walkable. Be discreet with cameras.
sights.q: Corviale, Via di Poggio Verde, Roma

sights.name: Laurentino 38 and its "bridges"
sights.blurb: A 1970s–80s estate on a 4 km ring road, crossed by "bridge-buildings" that were meant to hold shops and became Rome's most stigmatised addresses.
sights.when: Public streets. The first bridge is the Municipio IX office; bridges 5 and 6 are building sites.
sights.q: Viale Ignazio Silone, Laurentino 38

sights.name: Tuscolano: Libera's "horizontal unit" and the INA-Casa estate
sights.blurb: Adalberto Libera's walled "kasbah" of patio houses (1950–54), inside Rome's biggest INA-Casa estate, where Pasolini shot Mamma Roma.
sights.when: A lived-in courtyard entered through a vaulted gate on Via Selinunte; be discreet. The estate streets are public.
sights.q: Via Selinunte, Tuscolano, Roma

sights.name: Borgata Quarticciolo
sights.blurb: The last Fascist borgata (1940–43), laid out like a Roman army camp; its tower was the Fascist party house, then a police station.
sights.when: Public streets; included in Open House Roma.
sights.q: Piazza del Quarticciolo, Roma

sights.name: Villaggio Olimpico and the Corso Francia viaduct
sights.blurb: The 1960 athletes' village on pilotis, with Nervi's viaduct on "butterfly" piers carrying the road over it.
sights.when: Public streets; walk under the viaduct. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Viadotto di Corso Francia, Villaggio Olimpico, Roma

sights.name: Tor di Valle racecourse
sights.blurb: Julio Lafuente's 1959 grandstand of concrete "umbrellas", crumbling behind a broken wall since the racecourse closed in 2013.
sights.when: Not legally enterable: fenced, partly squatted, asbestos. View through gaps from Via del Mare / Via dell'Ippica.
sights.q: Ippodromo Tor di Valle, Roma

sights.name: Vela di Calatrava, Tor Vergata
sights.blurb: The 75 m white ribbed "sail" of Calatrava's unfinished swimming stadium, abandoned for 15 years and handed back to the city in 2025.
sights.when: The park is open; the structures by event only.
sights.q: Vela di Calatrava, Tor Vergata

sights.name: Stadio Flaminio
sights.blurb: Pier Luigi and Antonio Nervi's 1959 stadium, closed since 2011, with a cantilevered ribbed canopy behind fences and weeds.
sights.when: Closed; view from the street.
sights.q: Stadio Flaminio, Roma

sights.name: Palazzetto dello Sport
sights.blurb: Nervi and Vitellozzi's 1957 ribbed dome on Y-shaped buttresses, put up in 40 days from 1,620 precast pieces.
sights.when: Exterior always; interior at events.
sights.q: Palazzetto dello Sport, Piazza Apollodoro 10

sights.name: EUR: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana
sights.blurb: The "Square Colosseum" and the stripped-classical streets of the world's fair Mussolini never held.
sights.when: Streets always; the Palazzo's interior only during exhibitions (Fendi headquarters).
sights.q: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana, Quadrato della Concordia

sights.name: Foro Italico and Stadio dei Marmi
sights.blurb: Mussolini's sports forum: a marble stadium ringed by 60 colossal athletes and an obelisk still reading MUSSOLINI DUX.
sights.when: Open grounds; the stadium is often free to walk or run in.
sights.q: Stadio dei Marmi, Viale dei Gladiatori

sights.name: Ex Velodromo Olimpico crater
sights.blurb: The 1960 Olympic velodrome was blown up in 2008 with 120 kg of explosive; a fenced green void of 6.6 hectares is all that is left.
sights.when: Fence and street only.
sights.q: Viale della Tecnica, EUR

sights.name: The Termini–Centocelle railway
sights.blurb: The narrow-gauge "trenino giallo" of 1916 ran down the Via Casilina for 110 years; it closed for good in March 2026, and its tracks are already a ruin.
sights.when: Street; pin at Porta Maggiore, where the line ran under the Roman gate. Approximate.
sights.q: Porta Maggiore, Roma

sights.name: Ex Ospedale Forlanini
sights.blurb: A 1930s tuberculosis city of 280,000 m², closed in 2015, still paying huge water bills, now rented as a film set.
sights.when: Closed; exterior from the street. Pin approximate (next to the working San Camillo hospital).
sights.q: Ospedale Forlanini, Circonvallazione Gianicolense, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria della Pietà and the Museo della Mente
sights.blurb: Europe's largest asylum (1913): a park of numbered pavilions, some still derelict and painted by street artists, with a museum of the mind in Pavilion 6.
sights.when: Park open in daylight; museum Tue–Sat 9:00–16:00 (Google, 2026), booking advised.
sights.q: Museo Laboratorio della Mente, Piazza di Santa Maria della Pietà 5

sights.name: Ex Penicillina
sights.blurb: Italy's first penicillin plant, opened in 1950 with Alexander Fleming present; abandoned since 2006, sold in 2025, waiting for demolition.
sights.when: Closed and dangerous; exterior only from Via Tiburtina. Probably gone within a few years.
sights.q: Ex Penicillina, Via Tiburtina 1040

sights.name: Ex Mira Lanza
sights.blurb: An 1899 soap and chemical works by the Tiber: pyrite furnaces, burnt sheds and murals by Seth, about to become student housing.
sights.when: Exterior; Teatro India, in part of the old works, has events.
sights.q: Forni pirite ex Mira Lanza, Lungotevere Vittorio Gassman

sights.name: Gazometro and Ostiense
sights.blurb: The steel skeleton of Europe's largest gasholder of 1937, 90 m tall: the icon of industrial Rome.
sights.when: Seen from the street and from the Ponte della Scienza; the site opens a couple of times a year.
sights.q: Gazometro Ostiense, Via del Commercio

sights.name: Ex SNIA Viscosa and Lago Bullicante
sights.blurb: The ruins of a rayon factory, where builders broke into an aquifer in the 1990s and created a lake that is now a wild park.
sights.q: Lago Bullicante ex SNIA, Via di Portonaccio 230

sights.name: Forte Prenestino
sights.blurb: One of the 15 forts of 1877 round Rome, occupied since 1986 by a self-run social centre with markets, concerts and tunnels.
sights.when: Events, markets and concerts (Google: Tue–Sun from 11:00); check its channels.
sights.q: CSOA Forte Prenestino, Via Federico Delpino 187

sights.name: Villa Torlonia bunkers
sights.blurb: Mussolini's shelters under his residence: a wine cellar turned refuge and an armoured bunker left unfinished in 1943.
sights.when: Guided visits only, booking through 060608; mostly weekends; about €13–20; steep stairs.
sights.q: Villa Torlonia Bunker, Via Nomentana 70

sights.name: Fosse Ardeatine
sights.blurb: The caves where 335 men were shot in March 1944, under a single huge concrete slab: the most powerful concrete space in Rome.
sights.when: Free; Mon–Fri 8:30–15:00, Sat–Sun 8:30–16:30 (Google, 2026). Closed some holidays.
sights.q: Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine, Via Ardeatina 174

sights.name: Non-Catholic Cemetery
sights.blurb: A garden cemetery under the Pyramid of Cestius, with Keats, Shelley, Gramsci and a cat colony.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 9:00–16:30, Sun 9:00–12:30 (Google, 2026); free, donation expected (cash).
sights.q: Cimitero Acattolico, Via Caio Cestio 6

sights.name: Verano and the bombing of San Lorenzo
sights.blurb: A cemetery the size of a town, still scarred by the Allied bombs of 19 July 1943, next to the ruins of San Lorenzo.
sights.when: Daily 7:30–18:00 (Google, 2026); free. The Sovrintendenza runs guided routes on the bombing.
sights.q: Cimitero del Verano, Piazzale del Verano

sights.name: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale
sights.blurb: Italy's national library of 1975, institutional brutalism by Castellazzi, Dell'Anese and Vitellozzi.
sights.when: Mon–Thu 8:30–19:00, Fri 8:30–14:30 (Google, 2026); ID needed to register.
sights.q: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Roma, Viale Castro Pretorio 105

sights.name: Palazzo dello Sport, EUR
sights.blurb: Nervi and Piacentini's 1960 Olympic dome, now a concert arena.
sights.when: Interior only with an event ticket.
sights.q: Palazzo dello Sport, Piazzale Pier Luigi Nervi 1

sights.name: Cimitero Flaminio, Prima Porta
sights.blurb: Rome's biggest cemetery: 140 hectares and 37 km of roads with buses inside, and a garden where ashes are scattered.
sights.when: Open daily. Pin approximate.
sights.q: Cimitero Flaminio, Prima Porta

sights.name: Via Rasella bullet holes
sights.blurb: About a hundred bullet holes left on purpose in the walls of Via Rasella 139, from the German return fire after the partisan bomb of 23 March 1944.
sights.when: A public street, always visible. There is no plaque.
sights.q: Via Rasella 139, Roma

sights.name: Via Tasso 145: the SS prison
sights.blurb: The SS prison of occupied Rome, with the original cells and the prisoners' graffiti on the walls.
sights.when: Daily 9:00–19:00 (Google, 2026); free, donation welcome; groups of up to 10 every 30 minutes.
sights.q: Museo Storico della Liberazione, Via Tasso 145

sights.name: Largo di Torre Argentina
sights.blurb: Four Republican temples in a sunken square, the place where Caesar was stabbed, and a sanctuary for stray cats.
sights.when: Visible from the street any time. Walkways at ancient level Tue–Sun 9:30–16:00 in winter, to 19:00 in summer; from 18 Nov 2026 €9 (€14 with the VR show), €6 reduced. Entry from Via di San Nicola de' Cesarini.
sights.q: Largo di Torre Argentina

sights.name: Campo de' Fiori: Giordano Bruno
sights.blurb: The hooded statue stands where the Inquisition burned the philosopher Giordano Bruno on 17 February 1600.
sights.when: A public square; the market runs in the mornings.
sights.q: Monumento a Giordano Bruno, Campo de' Fiori

sights.name: Via Caetani: where Aldo Moro was found
sights.blurb: The plaque on the spot where the Red Brigades left the body of former prime minister Aldo Moro in a red Renault 4 on 9 May 1978.
sights.when: A public street.
sights.q: Targa Aldo Moro, Via Michelangelo Caetani 8

sights.name: Porta Pia breach
sights.blurb: Where Italian troops broke through the Aurelian Wall on 20 September 1870 and ended the pope's rule over Rome.
sights.when: Street; the memorial column stands beside the gate on Corso d'Italia.
sights.q: Porta Pia, Roma

sights.name: The Ghetto and the round-up of 16 October 1943
sights.blurb: Brass stones in the pavement name the Jews taken from these streets on 16 October 1943; the square in front of the Portico bears the date.
sights.when: Public streets.
sights.q: Portico d'Ottavia, Roma

sights.name: Matteotti abduction monument
sights.blurb: A bronze on the exact spot where Fascist squads seized the Socialist MP Giacomo Matteotti on 10 June 1924.
sights.when: Public riverside, always.
sights.q: Monumento a Giacomo Matteotti, Lungotevere Arnaldo da Brescia

sights.name: Teresa Gullace plaque, Viale Giulio Cesare
sights.blurb: Where a pregnant mother of five was shot by a German soldier on 3 March 1944, trying to reach her husband in the barracks: the real Pina of Roma città aperta.
sights.when: Street, at the corner of Via Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa.
sights.q: Viale Giulio Cesare, ex caserma 81° Fanteria, Roma

sights.name: Giorgiana Masi plaque, Ponte Garibaldi
sights.blurb: At the Trastevere end of the bridge, a plaque for the 19-year-old student shot in the back at a demonstration on 12 May 1977. No one was convicted.
sights.when: Public bridge.
sights.q: Ponte Garibaldi, Roma

sights.name: Ponte dell'Industria ("Ponte di Ferro")
sights.blurb: An 1863 iron bridge with a 1997 plaque for ten women said to have been shot on it in April 1944; historians now doubt the event happened.
sights.when: Public bridge, reopened in 2025.
sights.q: Ponte dell'Industria, Via del Porto Fluviale

sights.name: San Pietro in Montorio: the 1849 cannonball
sights.blurb: A French cannonball of June 1849 still stuck in the wall of the church, from the siege of the Roman Republic.
sights.when: Street (left flank of the church).
sights.q: Chiesa di San Pietro in Montorio

sights.name: Galleria Colonna: the cannonball on the stairs
sights.blurb: A French cannonball of 1849 lies on the marble steps of the great hall where it landed, in the palace where Roman Holiday ends.
sights.when: Friday and Saturday 9:30–13:00 (Google, 2026); paid.
sights.q: Galleria Colonna, Via della Pilotta 17

sights.name: Arco dei Banchi: the 1277 flood plaque
sights.blurb: In a dark archway by Ponte Sant'Angelo, Rome's oldest flood mark still in the street: a Latin slab for November 1277 with the water level cut in it.
sights.when: Always open.
sights.q: Arco dei Banchi, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria sopra Minerva: the flood ladder
sights.blurb: A ladder of flood plaques on the façade, 1422 to 1870, two minutes from the Pantheon. Galileo abjured in the convent next door.
sights.when: Façade always; church 8:00–20:00 weekdays (Google, 2026).
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria sopra Minerva

sights.name: Ripetta hydrometer and flood columns
sights.blurb: Two columns marked with the great floods, and the gauge whose zero is still the reference for every Tiber level in Rome.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Piazza del Porto di Ripetta

sights.name: Cloaca Maxima outlet
sights.blurb: The triple-ringed stone mouth of Rome's great sewer, about 2,100 years old, still in the river wall next to Ponte Rotto.
sights.when: Best seen from the quay or from Ponte Palatino.
sights.q: Ponte Palatino, Roma

sights.name: Fontana dell'Acqua Acetosa
sights.blurb: A 1661 fountain in a sunken hollow over a famous mineral spring, closed in the 1960s for pollution; Goethe is said to have drunk here.
sights.when: Open (gated at times); Monday from 10:00.
sights.q: Fontana dell'Acqua Acetosa, Roma

sights.name: Montecitorio obelisk and meridian
sights.blurb: The Egyptian obelisk that was the pointer of Augustus' giant sundial; a bronze line in the paving recalls it.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Obelisco di Montecitorio

sights.name: Santa Maria degli Angeli: the 1702 meridian
sights.blurb: A brass meridian line set in the floor in 1702 to check the calendar, inside Michelangelo's church made from the Baths of Diocletian.
sights.when: Daily 8:00–20:00 (Google, 2026); free. Best near noon.
sights.q: Basilica Santa Maria degli Angeli e dei Martiri

sights.name: Collegio Romano and the Calandrelli tower
sights.blurb: The Jesuits' university, where Angelo Secchi set his observatory on the piers meant for Sant'Ignazio's dome: Italy's meteorological office for decades.
sights.when: Street view.
sights.q: Piazza del Collegio Romano

sights.name: Via Panisperna: the "boys" who started the nuclear age
sights.blurb: The physics institute where Fermi, Majorana, Segrè and the others discovered slow neutrons in 1934; a plaque says they "opened the nuclear age to the world".
sights.when: Street; the Enrico Fermi museum inside is by booking only and hard to get into.
sights.q: Via Panisperna 89, Roma

sights.name: Via Margutta: the rubbish edict and Roman Holiday
sights.blurb: A papal marble edict threatening rubbish-dumpers with "lashes, the stocks and the wheel", in the artists' street where Gregory Peck lived in Roman Holiday.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Via Margutta, Roma

sights.name: Mastro Titta's house
sights.blurb: The 15th-century house in Borgo of Giovanni Battista Bugatti, the papal executioner who carried out over 500 sentences from 1796 to 1864.
sights.when: Street; no sign on the house.
sights.q: Casa di Mastro Titta, Vicolo del Campanile 4

sights.name: Pasquino
sights.blurb: A battered Hellenistic torso where Romans have pinned anonymous satire against popes and rulers since the 1500s.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Statua di Pasquino, Roma

sights.name: Villa Farnesina: the Landsknecht graffito of 1528
sights.blurb: Scratched into Peruzzi's painted columns by a soldier of the 1527 Sack of Rome: "why should I not laugh: the Landsknechts have made the pope run."
sights.when: Mon–Sat 9:00–13:15 (Google, 2026); paid.
sights.q: Villa Farnesina, Via della Lungara 230

sights.name: Pommidoro (Pasolini's last dinner)
sights.blurb: The San Lorenzo trattoria where Pasolini ate his last dinner on 1 November 1975; the cheque he paid with, never cashed, hangs on the wall.
sights.when: Evenings Mon–Thu, lunch and dinner Fri–Sat, closed Sunday (Google, 2026).
sights.q: Pommidoro, Piazza dei Sanniti 44, San Lorenzo

sights.name: Al Biondo Tevere
sights.blurb: A riverside trattoria of 1914 where Pasolini stopped with Pino Pelosi on his last night; Visconti filmed Bellissima here.
sights.when: Closed Monday (Google, 2026); phone ahead, 06 5741172.
sights.q: Al Biondo Tevere, Via Ostiense 178

sights.name: Necci dal 1924
sights.blurb: The Pigneto bar where Pasolini and his actors hung out while making Accattone (1961), under a fig tree.
sights.q: Necci dal 1924, Via Fanfulla da Lodi 68, Pigneto

sights.name: Caffè Rosati
sights.blurb: The Piazza del Popolo café where Moravia, Morante, Pasolini, Calvino, Flaiano and the painters of the 1950s held court.
sights.when: Daily 7:30–23:30; expensive, and reviews of the service are harsh.
sights.q: Caffè Rosati, Piazza del Popolo 5

sights.name: Biblioteca Angelica
sights.blurb: One of Europe's first public libraries (1604), with Vanvitelli's three-storey reading hall; it played the Vatican archive in Angels & Demons.
sights.when: Mon–Fri 9:00–13:30 (Google, 2026); reading by reservation; visitors see only part of the hall.
sights.q: Biblioteca Angelica, Piazza di Sant'Agostino 8

sights.name: Antica Libreria Cascianelli
sights.blurb: A bookshop behind Piazza Navona with furnishings unchanged since the 1830s; John Wick buys his maps here.
sights.q: Antica Libreria Cascianelli, Largo Febo 15

sights.name: Via Montecuccoli 17: Roma città aperta
sights.blurb: The doorway Anna Magnani's Pina runs out of, and the street where she is shot, in Rossellini's Roma città aperta (1945).
sights.when: Street; the porter of no. 17 keeps a small display.
sights.q: Via Raimondo Montecuccoli 17, Roma

sights.name: Via Francesco Crispi: Ladri di biciclette
sights.blurb: The exact spot where Antonio's bicycle is stolen in De Sica's Bicycle Thieves (1948), fixed by the columns of no. 18.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Via Francesco Crispi 18, Roma

sights.name: Trevi Fountain: La dolce vita
sights.blurb: Anita Ekberg's walk into the fountain, one of the few Dolce Vita scenes really shot on location: most of Via Veneto was a set.
sights.when: Seen from the piazza any time. Reaching the basin costs €2 for non-residents since 2 Feb 2026 (Mon and Fri 11:30–22:00, other days 9:00–22:00; free after 22:00 and for Rome residents). Sitting on the rim is fined.
sights.q: Fontana di Trevi

sights.name: Bocca della Verità: Roman Holiday
sights.blurb: The ancient drain cover where Gregory Peck fakes losing his hand to scare Audrey Hepburn.
sights.when: Small fee and a queue; church portico.
sights.q: Bocca della Verità, Santa Maria in Cosmedin

sights.name: Scalinata dei Borgia: John Wick 2
sights.blurb: The covered medieval stairway from Via Cavour up to San Pietro in Vincoli, where Wick and Cassian fight down the steps.
sights.when: Always open.
sights.q: Scalinata dei Borgia, Via Cavour 256

sights.name: Via dei Funari: the yellow Fiat of Mission: Impossible
sights.blurb: Where Ethan Hunt and Grace grab the little yellow Fiat 500 in Dead Reckoning (2023).
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Via dei Funari, Santa Caterina dei Funari, Roma

sights.name: Rear of the Vittoriano: the Continental (John Wick 2)
sights.blurb: The museum front behind the Vittoriano plays the Continental hotel of Rome in John Wick: Chapter 2.
sights.when: Exterior.
sights.q: Museo Centrale del Risorgimento, Roma

sights.name: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna: Rome playing New York
sights.blurb: The modern-art gallery whose steps and halls stand in for New York's Met in John Wick: Chapter 2.
sights.when: Museum hours, closed Monday.
sights.q: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna, Viale delle Belle Arti 131

sights.name: Museum of Roman Civilisation: Spectre's funeral
sights.blurb: The Fascist-era colonnade in EUR that became a cemetery for Bond's funeral scene, because the Verano said no.
sights.when: Exterior free; the museum has been closed for renovation.
sights.q: Museo della Civiltà Romana, Piazza Giovanni Agnelli 10

sights.name: San Luigi dei Francesi: Ripley's coin lights
sights.blurb: The church with three Caravaggios lit by a coin box: Tom Ripley feeds it in the 2024 Netflix series.
sights.when: Church hours; bring coins.
sights.q: San Luigi dei Francesi, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria del Popolo: Angels & Demons
sights.blurb: Dan Brown's first "altar of science", Raphael's Chigi chapel; the diocese refused filming, so the interior was a studio set.
sights.when: Church hours.
sights.q: Santa Maria del Popolo, Piazza del Popolo 12

sights.name: Torre della Scimmia (Hilda's tower)
sights.blurb: A medieval tower with a lamp lit before the Madonna on top: the home of Hilda in Hawthorne's The Marble Faun, and of a famous monkey legend.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Torre della Scimmia, Via dei Portoghesi

sights.name: Casa di Goethe
sights.blurb: The flat on the Corso where Goethe lived in 1786–88 with the painter Tischbein, the setting of his Italian Journey.
sights.when: Museum hours (check before going).
sights.q: Casa di Goethe, Via del Corso 18

sights.name: Via Merulana 219: Gadda's Pasticciaccio
sights.blurb: A plaque on the building where Gadda set the murder of That Awful Mess on Via Merulana (1957), Rome's great crime novel.
sights.when: Street. Pin approximate.
sights.q: Via Merulana 219, Roma

sights.name: Zerocalcare's mammoth, Rebibbia
sights.blurb: The 60 m² mural of a mammoth outside Rebibbia metro station by the comic artist Zerocalcare: "Welcome to Rebibbia".
sights.when: Always visible.
sights.q: Murale mammut Zerocalcare, Rebibbia

sights.name: Via del Pellegrino: the end of the Magliana gang's boss
sights.blurb: Where Enrico De Pedis, a boss of the Banda della Magliana, was shot on 2 February 1990; the gang behind Romanzo Criminale.
sights.when: Street. Pin approximate.
sights.q: Via del Pellegrino 65, Roma

sights.name: Santa Maria della Vittoria: Saint Victoria's body
sights.blurb: Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa, and a few steps away a whole martyr in a glass case: wax over a real skeleton, teeth and fingers showing through.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 7–12 and 16–18, Sun 9–12 and 16–18 (Google, 2026). Free; not during Mass.
sights.q: Santa Maria della Vittoria, Via XX Settembre 17

sights.name: Santa Francesca Romana: the saint's skeleton and Peter's knees
sights.blurb: Above the Forum, a crypt where Rome's patron of drivers lies as a skeleton in her nun's habit, and two stones said to carry Saint Peter's kneeprints.
sights.when: Daily 10–17 (Google, 2026); free. The crypt stairs are at the sides of the sanctuary.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Francesca Romana, Piazza di Santa Francesca Romana 4

sights.name: Santa Maria in Cosmedin: Saint Valentine's skull
sights.blurb: Past the Mouth of Truth queue, a skull in a flower crown with "Valentine" painted on the forehead. Ten or more churches claim him.
sights.when: Daily 9:30–18 (Google, 2026); free. Skip the Bocca queue: the church door is beside it.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria in Cosmedin

sights.name: St Peter's: popes in glass and Bernini's skeletons
sights.blurb: Three popes you can see through glass, and two Bernini tombs where a gilded skeleton writes a pope's name in the book of the dead.
sights.when: Daily 7–19:10 (Google, 2026); free, security queue; dress code (shoulders and knees).
sights.q: Basilica di San Pietro, Vatican

sights.name: Vatican Necropolis (Scavi): Peter's tomb
sights.blurb: A Roman street of tombs under St Peter's, ending at the place where bones claimed as the apostle's lie behind a wall.
sights.when: Guided only, about 250 people a day; book by email with the Ufficio Scavi (about €20, they set the date); closed Sunday; over-15s only (older source).
sights.q: Ufficio Scavi, Fabbrica di San Pietro, Vatican

sights.name: Chiesa Nuova: Philip Neri under a silver mask
sights.blurb: The Apostle of Rome lies in his chapel left of the high altar, his face covered by a silver mask; his rooms are next door.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 7:30–12 and 17–19:45, Sun 8–12 and 17–20 (Google, 2026). The saint's rooms have their own, shorter hours.
sights.q: Chiesa Nuova, Santa Maria in Vallicella

sights.name: Sant'Agnese in Agone: Agnes's head
sights.blurb: On Piazza Navona, the skull of the thirteen-year-old martyr, given by Pius X in 1900, kept in the Chapel of the Sacred Head; below, the arches of Domitian's stadium.
sights.when: Tue–Fri 9–13 and 15–19, Sat–Sun to 20; closed Mon (Google, 2026). A visitor reports the crypt closed at weekends.
sights.q: Sant'Agnese in Agone, Piazza Navona

sights.name: Il Gesù: Francis Xavier's forearm
sights.blurb: Above the right transept altar hangs the hand and forearm of the missionary who died off China in 1552; across the nave, Ignatius in a bronze urn.
sights.when: Mon–Fri 7:30–12:30 and 16:30–19:30, weekends a little longer (Google, 2026); free.
sights.q: Chiesa del Gesù, Piazza del Gesù

sights.name: Santa Maria Maggiore: Pius V in a crystal coffin
sights.blurb: In Sixtus V's chapel the body of the pope of Lepanto lies exposed in a crystal coffin; Pope Francis was buried in the same basilica in 2025.
sights.when: Daily 7–18:30 (Google, 2026); free, security check, dress code.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore

sights.name: Santa Croce in Gerusalemme: the Passion relics
sights.blurb: Helena's palace chapel: a finger said to be Thomas's, thorns, a nail, and the Title of the Cross, which carbon-dated to around 1000 AD.
sights.when: Daily 7:30–19 (Google, 2026); free. A visitor warns the relics chapel can close earlier than the church.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Croce in Gerusalemme

sights.name: Lateran: the sweating tomb of Sylvester II
sights.blurb: A slab behind a nave pillar of the pope's cathedral that, legend says, sweats and rattles before a pope dies.
sights.when: Daily 7–18:30 (Google, 2026); free.
sights.q: Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano

sights.name: Santa Sabina: the devil's stone
sights.blurb: A black basalt ball on a twisted column by the entrance: the devil threw it at Saint Dominic, says the legend; a Roman scale weight, say scholars.
sights.when: Tue–Sat 8–19, Sun–Mon from 12 (Google, 2026); free. Next to the Orange Garden.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Sabina, Aventino

sights.name: Santa Maria della Scala: Teresa of Ávila's foot
sights.blurb: In a Trastevere chapel, the right foot of Teresa of Ávila, cut from her body and sent to Rome in 1617; upstairs, the popes' old pharmacy.
sights.when: Daily 10–13 and 16–19 (Google, 2026). The relic travelled to Spain in summer 2026: check it is back.
sights.q: Santa Maria della Scala, Piazza della Scala 23

sights.name: San Francesco a Ripa: Bernini's dying Ludovica
sights.blurb: Bernini's last great statue: a widow-saint on her deathbed, clutching her breast, lit from a hidden window; her bones are in the altar below.
sights.when: Daily 7–12:30 and 16–19:30 (Google, 2026); free. The chapel's restoration is finished.
sights.q: San Francesco a Ripa, Piazza di San Francesco d'Assisi 88

sights.name: Sant'Andrea al Quirinale: Kostka on his deathbed
sights.blurb: Upstairs behind Bernini's oval church, the room where a 17-year-old novice died in 1568, with Legros' coloured-marble figure of him dying on the bed.
sights.when: Tue–Sun 9–12 and 15–18, closed Mon (Google, 2026). The rooms are reached from the sacristy; small offering.
sights.q: Sant'Andrea al Quirinale, Via del Quirinale 30

sights.name: Santa Maria del Popolo: Gisleni's skeleton
sights.blurb: An architect's self-designed tomb: a shrouded skeleton behind a grille, between a chrysalis and a butterfly; and Death in inlaid stone on the Chigi chapel floor.
sights.when: Mon–Sat roughly 8:30–12 and 16–18, Sun 16:30–18 (Google, 2026); a visitor found it shut in June 2026.
sights.q: Santa Maria del Popolo, Piazza del Popolo 12

sights.name: Gesù e Maria: Death with an hourglass
sights.blurb: On Via del Corso, a grinning robed skeleton holding an hourglass and the portrait of the man whose tomb it is.
sights.when: Hours not published; ask by phone (06 3613717). The monument is right of the entrance.
sights.q: Chiesa di Gesù e Maria, Via del Corso 45

sights.name: Sant'Agostino: Death outwitted
sights.blurb: A Baroque cardinal's tomb where a bag-of-bones Death gapes as Fame opens the coffin and an eagle escapes; plus Saint Monica's tomb and a Caravaggio.
sights.when: Daily 8–12:30 and 16–19:30 (Google, 2026); free.
sights.q: Basilica di Sant'Agostino in Campo Marzio

sights.name: San Lorenzo in Damaso: Bernini's flying skeleton
sights.blurb: Hidden inside the Cancelleria palace, a winged skeleton by Bernini's workshop hoists a dead man's portrait over a black marble curtain.
sights.when: Daily about 10:30–12:30 and 16–19 (Google, 2026). Enter from Piazza della Cancelleria; the monument is in the entrance hall.
sights.q: San Lorenzo in Damaso, Piazza della Cancelleria 1

sights.name: Santa Maria in Monterone: Death holds an empty tomb
sights.blurb: A small church off Largo Argentina where a winged skeleton guards the monument of an archbishop whose body went home to Genoa.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 7–12 and 16–19, closed Sun (Google, 2026). Where in the church: not checked.
sights.q: Santa Maria in Monterone, Via di Monterone 75

sights.name: San Pietro in Vincoli: the reaper and the chains
sights.blurb: Michelangelo's Moses, the chains of Peter, and two Baroque tombs where Death is a winged skeleton with a scythe or a pair of skeletons carrying a portrait.
sights.when: Mon–Sat 7:30–12:20 and 15–17:50, Sun from 9 (Google, 2026); free. Building works inside in 2026.
sights.q: Basilica di San Pietro in Vincoli

sights.name: Palazzo Massimo: the Grottarossa mummy
sights.blurb: The only known embalmed Roman: a girl of the 2nd century AD, found in 1964 by Via Cassia with her jointed doll and her jewels.
sights.when: Tue–Sun 9–19, closed Mon (Ministry of Culture, 2026); museum ticket. The mummy is in the basement with the coins and jewels.
sights.q: Museo Nazionale Romano, Palazzo Massimo, Largo di Villa Peretti 2

sights.name: Museo Criminologico (closed)
sights.blurb: Rome's crime museum, with the executioner Mastro Titta's red cloak, in an 1827 juvenile prison on Via Giulia. Shut for years.
sights.when: Closed for maintenance in 2026; the design contract for the works was reported awarded in Aug 2026, reopening years away. Outside only.
sights.q: Museo Criminologico, Via del Gonfalone 29

sights.name: Colosseum
sights.blurb: The Flavian amphitheatre, best seen from below: the hypogeum's lift shafts and the attic show how the show worked.
sights.when: 24h ticket €18; Full Experience €24 (arena, underground or attic), over 2 days. Tickets open 30 days ahead on ticketing.colosseo.it; on-site sales only at the Piazza del Colosseo office.
sights.q: Colosseo, Piazza del Colosseo

sights.name: Roman Forum
sights.blurb: The civic heart of Republican and imperial Rome; the SUPER sites (Curia floor, Romulus's bronze doors) are the ones to get inside.
sights.when: 24h Colosseum–Forum ticket, or Forum Pass SUPER €18 (no time slot; valid 30 days). SUPER sites and the Curia are shut on free first Sundays.
sights.q: Foro Romano, Largo della Salara Vecchia

sights.name: Palatine: Houses of Augustus and Livia
sights.blurb: Augustus's own rooms, painted in the 1st century BC: the room of masks and Livia's house on the hill where Rome began.
sights.when: SUPER sites only (Forum Pass SUPER or Full Experience). House of Augustus closed Mon, House of Livia closed Tue; shut on free first Sundays.
sights.q: Casa di Augusto, Palatino

sights.name: Capitoline Museums
sights.blurb: The world's oldest public museum: the bronze Marcus Aurelius, and a tunnel under the square to the Tabularium's arches over the Forum.
sights.when: Sovrintendenza museum; Rome residents free since Feb 2026. Check price and hours at museicapitolini.org.
sights.q: Musei Capitolini, Piazza del Campidoglio

sights.name: Circus Maximus
sights.blurb: A 600 m grassy valley that was Rome's chariot track; the excavated curved end and a medieval tower are what survive.
sights.when: Open field free; the archaeological south-east end is ticketed (Sovrintendenza).
sights.q: Circo Massimo

sights.name: Theatre of Marcellus
sights.blurb: An Augustan theatre whose upper floors became a Renaissance palace with private flats still lived in today.
sights.when: Exterior free; interior only for summer concerts.
sights.q: Teatro di Marcello

sights.name: Ara Pacis
sights.blurb: Augustus's Altar of Peace inside Richard Meier's 2006 pavilion; look for the small animals hidden in the acanthus scrolls.
sights.when: Sovrintendenza museum; check arapacis.it for hours and price.
sights.q: Museo dell'Ara Pacis

sights.name: Mausoleum of Augustus
sights.blurb: The largest round tomb of antiquity, still closed for its new museum; the rebuilt piazza steps down to the ancient ground level.
sights.when: Closed since June 2022. Works due to end "by the end of 2026"; no opening date, hours or price announced (Nov 2026).
sights.q: Mausoleo di Augusto, Piazza Augusto Imperatore

sights.name: Trajan's Markets
sights.blurb: Apollodorus's brick hemicycle of shops and offices; walk the basalt-paved Via Biberatica and look down on Trajan's Column.
sights.when: Museo dei Fori Imperiali (Sovrintendenza); hours not re-checked.
sights.q: Mercati di Traiano, Via IV Novembre 94

sights.name: Western Library of Trajan's Forum
sights.blurb: One of the twin library halls beside Trajan's Column, opened underground in November 2026 with its marble friezes and a videomapping show.
sights.when: Opened to the public 16 Nov 2026 (PNRR Caput Mundi). Hours not yet checked.
sights.q: Biblioteca occidentale del Foro di Traiano

sights.name: Domus Aurea
sights.blurb: Nero's buried Golden House under Colle Oppio: the Octagonal Room under its oculus and the vault mosaic of Ulysses and Polyphemus.
sights.when: Fri–Sun only, slots every 15 min about 9:00–16:30. €26 with tour + VR; €18 unguided at 12:00 and 17:00. Booking compulsory. NOT free on first Sundays. About 10 °C inside.
sights.q: Domus Aurea, Viale della Domus Aurea 1

sights.name: Baths of Trajan museum (Città Dipinta)
sights.blurb: A new museum under Colle Oppio for the "Painted City", a fresco of a whole city seen from above, and a newly found wall mosaic.
sights.when: Trial opening 12 Sep 2026 – 31 Mar 2027, pre-booked only.
sights.q: Museo delle Terme di Traiano, Colle Oppio

sights.name: Baths of Caracalla
sights.blurb: Enormous imperial baths; the prize is underground: cart-sized service tunnels, a mill and Rome's largest mithraeum.
sights.when: Day ticket about €8 (+€2 online). Underground and mithraeum only on special evenings (2026 season ended 15 Oct). Step-free entrance at Via Antonina 5.
sights.q: Terme di Caracalla, Viale delle Terme di Caracalla 52

sights.name: Porta San Sebastiano and Museum of the Walls
sights.blurb: The best-kept gate of the Aurelian Walls, with a walk along the top and a 1327 graffito of St Michael on the jamb.
sights.when: Sovrintendenza museum, usually free (verify).
sights.q: Museo delle Mura, Porta San Sebastiano

sights.name: Via Appia Antica, first miles
sights.blurb: The "queen of roads" out to Cecilia Metella: Quo Vadis and its footprints, catacombs, and original basalt paving.
sights.when: Road free; car traffic restricted on Sundays (verify). Appia park combined ticket for Cecilia Metella and Villa dei Quintili.
sights.q: Mausoleo di Cecilia Metella, Via Appia Antica

sights.name: St Peter's Square
sights.blurb: Bernini's colonnade, plus a sundial: the obelisk casts its noon shadow along a meridian line with zodiac discs set in the paving.
sights.when: Free and open.
sights.q: Piazza San Pietro

sights.name: St Peter's Basilica and dome
sights.blurb: The mother church: find the red porphyry disc inside the door, the length markers in the nave, and climb between the dome's two shells.
sights.when: Basilica and Grottoes free. Dome online at basilicasanpietro.va: €17 stairs (551 steps), €22 lift + 320 steps; kiosk prices disputed.
sights.q: Basilica di San Pietro

sights.name: Vatican Museums
sights.blurb: Beyond the Sistine Chapel: Danti's Gallery of Maps, the bronze pinecone, and the original Bramante spiral stair.
sights.when: €20 at the desk, €25 online (tickets.museivaticani.va only). Mon–Sat 8:00–20:00, last entry 18:00; free last Sunday 9:00–14:00. Closed other Sundays.
sights.q: Musei Vaticani, Viale Vaticano

sights.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
sights.blurb: Hadrian's tomb turned papal fortress: the ancient spiral ramp inside, Clement VII's painted bathroom, and the angel terrace.
sights.when: €18 from 1 Jul 2026, tickets carry your name. Closed Mon except the first Monday of the month 14:00–20:00, €5 (to end 2026).
sights.q: Castel Sant'Angelo

sights.name: Passetto di Borgo
sights.blurb: The 800 m covered corridor in the Leonine Wall that let Clement VII flee from the Vatican to the castle in 1527.
sights.when: Guided or timed visits only, Fri–Sun, booked on museiitaliani.it / CoopCulture: day guided €30, self-guided €24 (incl. castle); Sat evening €14–28. Not on first Sundays.
sights.q: Passetto di Borgo

sights.name: St John Lateran
sights.blurb: The cathedral of Rome: the octagonal baptistery, the Cosmatesque cloister, the tallest obelisk, and a fresco of the first Jubilee.
sights.when: Basilica free. Audio-guide combo €14 (€11 ages 6–17): cloister, baptistery, Scala Santa, Sancta Sanctorum and treasury.
sights.q: Arcibasilica di San Giovanni in Laterano

sights.name: Scala Santa and Sancta Sanctorum
sights.blurb: Twenty-eight marble steps venerated as Pilate's, climbed on the knees inside a walnut casing; the popes' private chapel at the top.
sights.when: Stairs free: 6:00–13:30 and 15:00–18:30 (Sun from 7:00). Sancta Sanctorum €3.50 cash, Mon–Sat about 9:30–13:00 and 15:00–17:10; closed Sun.
sights.q: Pontificio Santuario della Scala Santa

sights.name: Santa Maria Maggiore
sights.blurb: 5th-century mosaics, Bernini's family slab in the floor, Pope Francis's plain tomb, and a Roman farming calendar underground.
sights.when: Basilica free. Loggia and roof route €12 (€7 reduced). Underground by guided visit (booked on the Vatican Museums site, 50 min).
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore

sights.name: St Paul Outside the Walls
sights.blurb: Rebuilt after the 1823 fire: a mosaic portrait of every pope round the nave, Paul's sarcophagus under the altar, and a Vassalletto cloister.
sights.when: Basilica free; cloister small fee.
sights.q: Basilica di San Paolo fuori le Mura

sights.name: Pantheon
sights.blurb: Hadrian's temple and the largest unreinforced concrete dome: the oculus light, the floor drains under it, Raphael's tomb.
sights.when: €7 since 1 Jul 2026 (€2 EU 18–25; under 18 and Rome residents free). Daily 9:00–19:00, last entry 18:30, ticket office closes 18:00. Book a slot on Musei Italiani; first Sundays free, queue only.
sights.q: Pantheon, Piazza della Rotonda

sights.name: Piazza Navona
sights.blurb: A Baroque square on the exact plan of Domitian's stadium, with Bernini's Four Rivers in the middle.
sights.when: Open.
sights.q: Piazza Navona

sights.name: Stadium of Domitian
sights.blurb: The arcades of the AD 86 stadium, 4.5 m under the street behind Piazza Navona.
sights.when: Via di Tor Sanguigna 3; price and hours not re-checked.
sights.q: Stadio di Domiziano, Via di Tor Sanguigna 3

sights.name: Spanish Steps and the Barcaccia
sights.blurb: De Sanctis's 1720s staircase up to Trinità dei Monti; the boat fountain at the foot is sunk because the water pressure was low.
sights.when: Open; sitting on the steps is banned and fined.
sights.q: Scalinata di Trinità dei Monti

sights.name: Trinità dei Monti: the anamorphoses
sights.blurb: Inside the convent above the Spanish Steps: optical-science murals that only resolve from one spot, and a sundial made with mirrors.
sights.when: Guided visits only, by booking: secretariat.tdm@emmanuelco.org, +39 06 6794179.
sights.q: Trinità dei Monti

sights.name: Quirinal Palace
sights.blurb: The popes' summer palace, then the kings', now the President's: the Cortile d'Onore and the state rooms.
sights.when: Booking ≥5 days ahead at visite.quirinale.it, €2.50 per route; ID matching the booking. Tours in Italian. Closed days disputed (Mon and Tue vs Mon and Thu). Visits can be cancelled for state business.
sights.q: Palazzo del Quirinale

sights.name: Galleria Borghese
sights.blurb: Bernini's marble at its most alive (Pluto's fingers in Proserpina's thigh), six Caravaggios, and a picture store you can book.
sights.when: Booking compulsory (+39 06 32810), 2-hour timed slots; closed Mon. Free first Sunday, booking opens 10 days before.
sights.q: Galleria Borghese, Piazzale Scipione Borghese 5

sights.name: Palazzo Massimo (National Roman Museum)
sights.blurb: Livia's painted garden room, a whole room of fruit trees and birds; and the bronze Boxer at Rest with copper blood.
sights.when: Museo Nazionale Romano; hours not re-checked.
sights.q: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme

sights.name: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
sights.blurb: A princely picture collection still owned by the family; Velázquez's Innocent X hangs with Bernini's bust of the same pope.
sights.when: Via del Corso 305; hours not re-checked.
sights.q: Galleria Doria Pamphilj, Via del Corso 305

sights.name: Palazzo Barberini
sights.blurb: The Barberini palace: two great staircases, Bernini's square and Borromini's oval, and Pietro da Cortona's ceiling. Built partly with Colosseum stone.
sights.when: Gallerie Nazionali; hours not re-checked. Garden mithraeum on rare visits only.
sights.q: Palazzo Barberini, Via delle Quattro Fontane 13

sights.name: Vittoriano: Terrazza delle Quadrighe
sights.blurb: The white monument everyone mocks gives the best 360° view over the centre, from its top terrace.
sights.when: VIVE ticket €18 (7 days, includes Palazzo Venezia); 9:30–19:30.
sights.q: Vittoriano, Terrazza delle Quadrighe

sights.name: Sapienza: the Città Universitaria
sights.blurb: Piacentini's 1935 campus: Sironi's mural uncovered from its postwar overpaint, Ponti's maths building, Pagano's physics.
sights.when: Grounds open by day. Sapienza Tour Mon–Fri 9–18, €5, booking (+39 06 49690304).
sights.q: Città Universitaria, Piazzale Aldo Moro 5

sights.name: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane
sights.blurb: Borromini's first church, small enough to fit inside one of St Peter's piers; the dome's shrinking coffers fake its height.
sights.when: Church hours; cloister and crypt hours not checked.
sights.q: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane

sights.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
sights.blurb: One of Rome's oldest Marian churches: ancient granite columns that don't match, a 12th-century apse mosaic and Cavallini's panels.
sights.when: Church hours.
sights.q: Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere

sights.name: Bone crypt of the Sacre Stimmate
sights.blurb: Under an 18th-century church by Largo Argentina: a restored crypt decorated with human bones and faux-marble frescoes.
sights.when: Free openings on Thursdays 15:00–20:00 on 26 Nov, 3 and 10 Dec 2026; after that unknown. Church open Mon–Sat mornings.
sights.q: Chiesa delle Sacre Stimmate di San Francesco, Largo delle Stimmate 1

sights.name: Vicus Caprarius: City of Water
sights.blurb: Eight metres under a cinema near the Trevi: a Hadrianic water tank of the Aqua Virgo, still taking water 2,000 years on.
sights.when: Tue–Sun 11:00–16:30, closed Mon (verify on vicuscaprarius.com).
sights.q: Vicus Caprarius, Vicolo del Puttarello 25

sights.name: Fontanone dell'Acqua Paola
sights.blurb: The show-end of Paul V's aqueduct on the Gianicolo; it drove Rome's first hydroelectric plant, and the garden behind it was the water's first sorting tank.
sights.when: Front always open. Rear garden by booking (060608) or on free sunset openings (late Aug–Sep 2026).
sights.q: Fontana dell'Acqua Paola, Via Garibaldi

sights.name: Moses Fountain (Acqua Felice)
sights.blurb: The end of Sixtus V's 1587 aqueduct, the first new water to the hills since antiquity, with its famously ugly Moses.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Fontana del Mosè, Piazza di San Bernardo

sights.name: Porta Maggiore
sights.blurb: Where two Roman aqueducts cross two roads, with a baker's tomb shaped like his ovens and trams running through.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Porta Maggiore

sights.name: Monte Testaccio
sights.blurb: An artificial hill of about 53 million broken oil jars, stacked in datable layers: ancient Rome's rubbish tip.
sights.when: Climbs on the Sovrintendenza calendar, book 060608, max 30.
sights.q: Monte Testaccio

sights.name: Porticus Aemilia
sights.blurb: Tufa walls of a vast Republican warehouse among Testaccio's apartment blocks: the river port's storage.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Porticus Aemilia, Via Florio

sights.name: Museo della Forma Urbis
sights.blurb: The fragments of the Severan marble map of Rome, laid over Nolli's 1748 map so you can walk ancient and modern Rome at once.
sights.when: Tue–Sun 10:00–16:00; €9 non-residents. Celio park free.
sights.q: Museo della Forma Urbis, Viale del Parco del Celio 20

sights.name: Museum of Pathological Anatomy
sights.blurb: In the Policlinico Umberto I: about 900 untreated heart defects and other specimens, shown to students for a century.
sights.when: Booking only (cira.digioia@uniroma1.it). Use the Policlinico entrance by the metro.
sights.q: Museo di Anatomia Patologica, Viale Regina Elena 324

sights.name: Primo Levi Museum of Chemistry
sights.blurb: Cannizzaro's instruments and Blanc's radioactivity kit, on the ground floor of Sapienza's chemistry building.
sights.when: Mon–Thu 9:00–13:00, free; afternoons on request. Cases visible from the atrium.
sights.q: Museo di Chimica Primo Levi, Piazzale Aldo Moro 5

sights.name: Museum of the History of Medicine (Arte Sanitaria)
sights.blurb: In the Santo Spirito hospital: Lelli's anatomical waxes, a 17th-century pharmacy, Mameli's dissection table.
sights.q: Museo Storico Nazionale dell'Arte Sanitaria, Lungotevere in Sassia 3

sights.name: Ex Mattatoio, Testaccio
sights.blurb: Ersoch's 1888–91 slaughterhouse, with the overhead meat rails and weighing machines still in place; now university, art and markets.
sights.when: Open; some pavilions derelict.
sights.q: Ex Mattatoio, Piazza Orazio Giustiniani

sights.name: Mercato Metronio
sights.blurb: A 1950s market by Di Fausto with Riccardo Morandi's double helical car ramp spiralling up to a garage on the roof.
sights.when: Under works; traders in temporary stalls outside; new market due end 2026–2027. Exterior only.
sights.q: Mercato Metronio, Via Magna Grecia

sights.name: Acqua Vergine arches, Via del Nazareno
sights.blurb: Three arches of the Aqua Virgo with Claudius's inscription, inside a courtyard off a side street near the Trevi.
sights.when: Through a courtyard gate at Via del Nazareno 14; more raised arches in Via del Bufalo.
sights.q: Via del Nazareno 14

sights.name: Quattro Fontane crossroads
sights.blurb: Sixtus V's crossroads: four corner fountains and, down three streets, three obelisks plus Porta Pia in one turn of the head.
sights.when: Traffic island; take care.
sights.q: Quattro Fontane

sights.name: Ponte Sisto and the Paola fountain
sights.blurb: Sixtus IV's 1475 bridge; the Paola water crosses inside it, and from here its fountain at Piazza Trilussa stacks under the Gianicolo's Fontanone.
sights.when: Street.
sights.q: Ponte Sisto

sights.name: Aventine keyhole and the Orange Garden
sights.blurb: A keyhole in the Knights of Malta's gate frames the dome of St Peter's at the end of a garden avenue.
sights.when: Free; expect a queue.
sights.q: Buco della Serratura, Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta

sights.name: Via Alessandrina over the fora
sights.blurb: A 1580s street kept as a walkway between the fora of Trajan and Augustus, beside Mussolini's 1932 cut.
sights.when: Free; CArMe works 2025–27, some sectors fenced.
sights.q: Via Alessandrina, Fori Imperiali

sights.name: Gianicolo terrace and the noon cannon
sights.blurb: The widest view over the centre; at noon a cannon fires below the terrace, as it has since 1904.
sights.when: Daily at 12:00; free. Arrive a little early.
sights.q: Il Cannone del Gianicolo

sights.name: Biblioteca Casanatense
sights.blurb: A Dominican library of 1701 beside the Minerva: the great reading hall with its two 18th-century globes.
sights.when: Salone on events and booked visits (+39 06 69760300).
sights.q: Biblioteca Casanatense, Via di Sant'Ignazio 52

sights.name: Biblioteca Vallicelliana and the Oratory
sights.blurb: Borromini's Salone for the Oratorians: two rows of pillars, galleries of books, and a façade that curves like open arms.
sights.when: Salone free Mon, Tue, Fri 10:00–13:00; Wed–Thu 15:00–18:00 by booking (b-vall.didattica@cultura.gov.it). Closed weekends.
sights.q: Biblioteca Vallicelliana, Piazza della Chiesa Nuova 18

sights.name: Bibliotheca Hertziana (Palazzo Zuccari)
sights.blurb: A doorway and windows shaped as monster mouths on Via Gregoriana; inside, a modern library built in the old shell.
sights.when: Street free; 45-minute researcher tours (biblhertz.it).
sights.q: Palazzo Zuccari, Via Gregoriana 28

sights.name: Ospedale delle Bambole (Doll Hospital)
sights.blurb: A tiny repair shop on Via di Ripetta whose window is full of doll heads, limbs and eyes waiting to be mended.
sights.q: Ospedale delle Bambole, Via di Ripetta 29

sights.name: Fountain of the Naiads
sights.blurb: The show-end of the Acqua Marcia (1870) in Piazza della Repubblica, with Rutelli's bronze nymphs that scandalised Rome in 1901.
sights.when: Street, always open.
sights.q: Fontana delle Naiadi, Piazza della Repubblica

sights.name: Pincio terrace
sights.blurb: Valadier's terrace over Piazza del Popolo: the three straight streets of the Tridente spreading south below you.
sights.when: Free.
sights.q: Terrazza del Pincio

sights.name: Piazza Sempione and the garden city
sights.blurb: Sabbatini's arcaded square of 1923 at the heart of Montesacro's garden city, with the tufa-faced town hall looking down the axis to the Aniene bridge.
sights.when: Street; the municipio is inside the Palazzo Pubblico, the arcades are public. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Piazza Sempione, Roma

sights.name: Villini of the Città Giardino Aniene
sights.blurb: The 1921–23 villini around the square, with stair towers, tufa walls and tiled roofs; about half the originals are left.
sights.when: Street only. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Città Giardino Aniene villini, Montesacro, Roma

sights.name: Ex GIL Montesacro (Palestra Agnini)
sights.blurb: A 1934 rationalist youth-movement building by Minnucci, clad in 2 cm of Carrara marble and still used as a gym.
sights.when: Working gym, so inside only by asking at the door; judge it from the street. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Palestra F. Agnini già GIL, Viale Adriatico 136, Roma

sights.name: Ponte Nomentano
sights.blurb: A Roman bridge over the Aniene with a medieval tower and a crenellated house on top, where Charlemagne is said to have met Pope Leo III.
sights.when: Open day and night; pedestrian only. A locked gate on the south side blocks the path to the nature reserve, so the walk on south needs a detour (Google review). Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Ponte Nomentano, Roma

sights.name: Monte Sacro and Parco Bolívar
sights.blurb: A small hill with two famous oaths: the plebs' strike of 494 BC and Simón Bolívar's vow of 1805 to free South America.
sights.when: Free park; the Bolívar bust has been vandalised several times (2014, 2024). Pin from Google Places (the park at Via Monte Serrone).
sights.q: Parco Simón Bolívar, Via Monte Serrone, Roma

sights.name: Tufello's comb blocks
sights.blurb: Twenty 'comb' blocks of 1940–47 by Sforza, one of Rome's twelve official borgate, built for families moved out of the centre.
sights.when: Street and courtyards; people live here. Pin from Google Places (Piazza degli Euganei).
sights.q: Piazza degli Euganei, Tufello, Roma

sights.name: Via di Valle Melaina blocks
sights.blurb: Blocks of 1932–33 built for families evicted when the Spina di Borgo was demolished for the Via della Conciliazione.
sights.when: Street. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Via di Valle Melaina, Roma

sights.name: Tufello's four martyrs and the 'Benvenuti' mural
sights.blurb: A plaque, stumbling stones and a welcome mural on Via Scarpanto for four antifascists from the quarter.
sights.when: Street. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Via Scarpanto, Tufello, Roma

sights.name: Ladri di biciclette: Via del Gran Paradiso and Parco Jonio
sights.blurb: The labour office where De Sica's bicycle thief begins, now with a 2014 plaque, and a park wall painted as a film strip of the movie.
sights.when: Street and park. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Via del Gran Paradiso, Roma

sights.name: Santissimo Redentore a Val Melaina
sights.blurb: A 1975–78 church whose pillars alternate travertine and peperino like layers of rock.
sights.when: Mass hours.
sights.q: Santissimo Redentore a Val Melaina, Via Monte Ruggero 63, Roma

sights.name: Sant'Achille, Talenti
sights.blurb: A 1970–73 church by Giorgio Guidi, planned like a theatre around the altar.
sights.when: Mass hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Sant'Achille, Via Gaspara Stampa 64, Roma

sights.name: Quartiere Coppedè
sights.blurb: Gino Coppedè's fairy-tale quarter of 1915–27 around Piazza Mincio, with a chandelier hung under the arch and twelve frogs in the fountain.
sights.when: Street; always open. Pin from Google Places (Villini delle Fate).
sights.q: Quartiere Coppedè, Piazza Mincio, Roma

sights.name: Mercato Nomentano
sights.blurb: Elena Luzzatto's first work, a 1928–29 market hall whose reliefs of produce and a Roman wolf still show the gaps left by the Fascist symbols removed in 1946.
sights.when: Market stalls Mon–Fri 7:30–19:30, Sat 7:30–15:30, closed Sun (Google, Nov 2026). Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Mercato Nomentano, Piazza Alessandria, Roma

sights.name: Sedia del Diavolo
sights.blurb: A tomb of the mid-2nd century whose collapsed front left a stone 'chair', now on a traffic island in Piazza Elio Callistio.
sights.when: Street; viewed from the pavement. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Sedia del Diavolo, Piazza Elio Callistio, Roma

sights.name: Museo di Antropologia Sergi
sights.blurb: A small university museum that holds the two Saccopastore Neanderthal skulls, found in a pit on the Aniene in 1929 and 1935.
sights.when: Mon, Thu, Fri 9–13; Tue, Wed 9–17; closed Sat–Sun (Google, Nov 2026); afternoons by booking. Whether the skulls are on show or casts is unconfirmed. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Museo di Antropologia G. Sergi, Piazzale Aldo Moro 5, Roma

sights.name: Istituto Superiore di Sanità and its museum
sights.blurb: Amendola's 1931–34 institute with Nicolini's 1950 relief of Science, and a museum of old physics instruments and public health.
sights.when: Museum renewed in July 2026; visits by booking (museo@iss.it); reduced ticket €3.
sights.q: Istituto Superiore di Sanità, Viale Regina Elena 299, Roma

sights.name: Sant'Agnese fuori le mura
sights.blurb: A 7th-century basilica with a gold apse mosaic, reached by a stair lined with ancient inscriptions, beside the catacomb of St Agnes.
sights.when: Daily 7:30–12:00 and 15:00–19:30 (Google); the catacomb is by guided visit. Pair with Santa Costanza next door. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Basilica di Sant'Agnese fuori le mura, Via Nomentana 349, Roma

sights.name: Casa del Girasole
sights.blurb: Moretti's 1947–50 block whose front splits and rotates like a sunflower, over a rough rusticated base.
sights.when: Private flats; best seen from the pavement opposite. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Casa del Girasole, Viale Bruno Buozzi 64, Roma

sights.name: Villa Glori
sights.blurb: The park where Enrico Cairoli and his Garibaldian volunteers fell on 23 October 1867, marked by a brick plinth where an almond tree stood.
sights.when: Park open 7:00 to dusk.
sights.q: Villa Glori, Piazzale del Mandorlo, Roma

sights.name: Villa Ada: where Mussolini was arrested
sights.blurb: The royal park where Victor Emmanuel III received Mussolini on 25 July 1943 and had him arrested on the forecourt.
sights.when: Park free. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Villa Ada Savoia, Roma

sights.name: Villa Ada royal bunker
sights.blurb: The Savoy family's air-raid shelter: seven rooms in a ring to deflect blast, a vehicle tunnel, and a mushroom-shaped escape hatch.
sights.when: Reopened 27 Feb 2026; guided tours only, book first (bunkervillaada.it; Via Salaria 267). Price sources disagree (€10/€15 vs €13/€19). 14–17 °C inside. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Bunker Villa Ada Savoia, Via Salaria 267, Roma

sights.name: Guido Reni district
sights.blurb: Twenty-three sheds of a 1906 military electrical and precision-instrument works, now used for exhibitions and slated for demolition.
sights.when: Exhibition venue; the district is open Tue–Sun 10–20 (Google) but not demolished yet in Nov 2026. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Guido Reni District, Via Guido Reni 7, Roma

sights.name: Auditorium Parco della Musica and its Roman villa
sights.blurb: Piano's concert halls, built after the diggers found a 6th-century BC farmhouse and moved the halls to avoid it.
sights.when: Foyer and the small free museum open daily 11–18 (Google); concerts ticketed. Pin from Google Places.
sights.q: Auditorium Parco della Musica, Via Pietro de Coubertin 30, Roma

sights.name: Ponte Milvio
sights.blurb: Rome's oldest standing bridge, from 109 BC (only the three central arches are Roman), with Valadier's tower and the stray love-lock padlocks.
sights.when: Open at all times.
sights.q: Ponte Milvio, Roma

sights.name: Santa Chiara a Vigna Clara
sights.blurb: A 1960–62 church of two off-centre drums, with the windows grouped into three crosses and radial roof beams.
sights.when: Mass hours.
sights.q: Chiesa di Santa Chiara, Vigna Clara, Roma

sights.name: Castel Giubileo dam
sights.blurb: Minnucci's hydroelectric dam on the Tiber, opened 12 May 1951 (17 MW), where a siren sounds when the gates are opened.
sights.when: Seen from the river banks or the ring road.
sights.q: Diga di Castel Giubileo, Roma

sights.name: Fidenae: the cut and the collapsed amphitheatre
sights.blurb: The hill of an ancient town, cut by the railway trench, where in AD 27 a badly built amphitheatre collapsed, killing or injuring tens of thousands.
sights.when: Street. Map pin approximate.
sights.q: Fidene, Villa Spada, Roma

sights.name: Aeroporto dell'Urbe
sights.blurb: Rome's 1928 seaplane and light-plane airfield on the Tiber, where Nuvolari raced a plane in 1931 and which was bombed on 19 July 1943.
sights.when: Working airfield; the railwaymen's plaque was not found.
sights.q: Aeroporto dell'Urbe, Roma

sights.name: Stazione Farneto
sights.blurb: A railway station built for the 1990 World Cup and used for just eight days.
sights.when: Now an emergency access to the Cassia–Monte Mario tunnel; exterior only.
sights.q: Stazione Farneto, Roma

sights.name: Forte Antenne
sights.blurb: An 1880s fort inside Villa Ada, built on the archaic walls of the ancient town of Antemnae.
sights.when: Event concession ran to 31 Oct 2026; what happens after is unknown. Check before going.
sights.q: Forte Antenne, Via del Forte Antenne 12, Roma

sights.name: Saxa Rubra: kiln and Roman road at the RAI
sights.blurb: A Roman kiln, a round-drum tomb and a stretch of the Flaminia's basalt paving beside the 1990 RAI broadcasting centre.
sights.when: Visible from the street at the RAI entrance on Via Carlo Emery; a restoration project is under way (2026). Map pin approximate.
sights.q: RAI Saxa Rubra, Via Teulada, Roma

sights.name: Villa di Livia at Prima Porta
sights.blurb: Livia's villa, where the painted garden room that is now in Palazzo Massimo was found; the site has full-size copies of the frescoes.
sights.when: Reopened after restoration (a free open day 26–27 Sep 2026); regular opening days not confirmed. Check with Parco archeologico before going.
sights.q: Villa di Livia, Prima Porta, Roma

sights.name: Arco di Malborghetto
